title: Asymmetric kernel election and token-prefetch bundler for multi-GPU rendezvous
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce 95th-percentile end-to-end latency for medium-length (~512 tokens) prefill+decode workloads on heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters. Approach combines an asymmetric kernel-election policy (device-aware, sequence-length-aware kernel choice + fallback rules) with a token-prefetch bundler that batches rendezvous windows to maximize NCCL overlap during prefill while avoiding decode stalls. This ticket scopes design, prototype implementation in the runtime, and a controlled perf experiment on staging cluster.
proposed_design: Asymmetric kernel election: runtime maintains per-device kernel profiles (latency, memory, prefetched-KV footprint) for FP16/FP8/fused-mha/fused-gemm variants. At request arrival, the electors choose a primary kernel and up to one fast fallback kernel; selection is weighted by sequence-length buckets and estimated KV-cache residency. Election happens per-stage (tensor/pipeline stage) to allow hetero-device choices.

Token-prefetch bundler (TPB): instead of strictly aligning microbatches, TPB opens short rendezvous windows (configurable 1-4ms) that collect tokens from inflight prefill microbatches and issues a bundled prefetch pass. TPB emits phasing hints to NCCL layer so that comms for prefill can be overlapped with kernel execution in downstream stages. The bundler supports 'latency-first' and 'throughput-first' modes selectable by policy.

NCCL-overlap orchestration: introduce per-stage comm scheduling with priority lanes. Prefill comms are tagged opportunistically so NCCL can stream them concurrently with decode collectives where hardware supports it (NVLink/P2P). On topologies that block overlap, TPB reduces bundle size and opportunistically falls back to staggered rendezvous to avoid head-of-line stalls.

Attention optimizations: integrate selective FlashAttention variants based on sequence length and available workspace. For long sequences, use chunked attention with KV stripe alignment to improve cache reuse. Kernel election includes a 'kv-friendly' metric to prefer kernels that reduce cross-stage comm amplification.

Backpressure and safety: decode path remains conservative: if prefill bundling risks violating LTRL (latency SLO) the runtime switches to decode-optimized mode that minimizes prefill batching. Add circuit-breaker metrics and fallbacks (model-variant routing) to preserve correctness and quality.

Telemetry and rollouts: attach per-request traces: chosen kernel ids per stage, bundle id, NCCL queue occupancy, and observed overlap time. Feature gated behind runtime flag and a canary rollout with 5% traffic by default.
Compatibility: no model rewrite required. Works with existing model artifacts; requires runtime image bump for kernel table and NCCL hooks.

experiments: Experiment A (staging-hetero-1): 128 A100 + 64 A10g mix, baseline vs TPB latency/throughput. Measure p50/p95/p99 prefill, decode tail, overlap fraction reported by NCCL counters.

Experiment B (nvlink-disabled): simulate topologies without NVLink to validate graceful fallback to staggered rendezvous. Expect some degradation; acceptance if no regression >5% against baseline p95.
Experiment C (vary-window): sweep TPB windows [1ms,2ms,4ms,8ms] to find knee for mixed traffic. Record token latency and batch size distribution.
Experiment D (throughput-heavy): evaluate throughput-first mode with 100 concurrent streams and measure effective tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
Experiment E (quality-safety): validate no change in model outputs for canonical eval prompts across kernel variants. Run eval harness on 1000 prompt sets and compare embedding/text diffs.
Instrumentation: add per-bundle histogram for comm overlap and per-stage kernel latency traces to perf-dashboard (Grafana link in links).
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end prefill+first-decode token reduced by >=15% on staging-hetero-1 for sequence length 512 at default canary config
No model output regressions detected in the eval harness (statistical significance threshold alpha=0.01)
CPU/GPU memory safety: no OOMs observed in 3-hour soak on staging cluster
Canary rollout to 25% passes with <2% error-rate increase and cost-per-token delta <= +3%
Telemetry ready: bundle traces, kernel-choice per-stage, overlap fraction visible in dashboard
